title: The balance sheet and statement links
goal: Prepare a classified balance sheet and reconcile equity to the retained earnings statement.

slides.title: What does the business have and owe at this date?

items.heading: Resources
items.text: Cash, receivables, inventory, insurance, and the van.

items.heading: Claims
items.text: Obligations to others and the owners’ residual interest.

slides.takeaway: The balance sheet reports position at a date.
slides.notes: Use the June 30 balances, including ending retained earnings.

slides.title: Distinguish current and noncurrent assets

rows: Other resources held for long-term use
Insurance used in the coming year

slides.takeaway: Apply the operating cycle or one-year horizon appropriate to the item.
slides.notes: The normal operating cycle can exceed one year for inventory and trade receivables. For other items consider realization or use within 12 months; cash restrictions also matter. Our case has a simple one-year cycle.

slides.title: Distinguish current and noncurrent liabilities

rows: Note principal due in next 12 months

slides.takeaway: A loan can have both current and noncurrent portions.
slides.notes: The remaining note is $11,500. Twelve $500 principal payments make $6,000 current. Actual terms and rights to defer settlement matter in fuller reporting.

slides.title: Show contributed capital and retained earnings
slides.notes: Do not add Owner’s Capital, Owner’s Investment, or current net income again.

slides.title: Build the classified balance sheet
slides.lead: Summit Trail Co. · Balance sheet · June 30 · USD
slides.notes: Vehicle remains at cost in the no-adjustments exercise. Do not describe this simplified statement as fully standards-compliant.

slides.title: Trace net income through retained earnings to equity
slides.takeaway: Profit enters ending equity through retained earnings.
slides.notes: Link statement cells instead of retyping amounts.

slides.title: A balanced equation is necessary but not sufficient

blocks.text: A $600 equipment purchase is incorrectly recorded as Rent Expense.

rows: Net income and ending equity understated

slides.takeaway: The equation can balance when both sides are wrong.
slides.notes: Cash was credited correctly. Missing equipment understates assets; overstated expense understates equity.

slides.title: Try it: resolve a statement-linking error
slides.lead: A student adds net income separately to ending retained earnings. What is wrong?
slides.notes: Fix the statement link; no journal entry is needed for a presentation formula error.

blocks.text: The extra $3,440 repeats net income already included in ending retained earnings.

slides.title: Check the date, cash balance, and total equity

items: Use the same company and reporting date.
Cash matches the ledger and trial balance.
Current debt follows the repayment terms.

slides.takeaway: Week 11 will reconcile cash to the cash flow statement.
slides.notes: Supports Balance_Sheet. Check inventory and prepaid insurance have not been expensed or counted twice.
